cosy-lesson.title: "The amount of beautiful things in your life depends on your ability to notice them.": Anonymous

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Appreciate – to recognize the full worth, quality, or value of something deeply.

p.em: Example: We must learn to slow down and appreciate the simple, quiet moments of our day.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mindfulness – the mental state of being fully conscious and aware of the present moment.

p.em: Example: Practicing daily mindfulness helps reduce stress and improves our concentration.

cosy-blockquote.p: To notice – to become aware of or pay active attention to someone or something around you.

p.em: Example: If you walk too fast, you will fail to notice the lovely autumn leaves on the street.

cosy-blockquote.p: Joy – a feeling of great pleasure, delight, and happiness.

p.em: Example: Hearing her child's honest laughter filled her mind with pure, genuine joy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Presence – the state or fact of existing, occurring, or being fully present in a place.

p.em: Example: Real presence requires putting away your phone to listen to your partner carefully.

cosy-blockquote.p: Aesthetic – concerned with beauty, art, or the appreciation of physical and natural beauty.

p.em: Example: She loved the quiet, ancient aesthetic of the old coffee shops in Paris.

cosy-blockquote.p: To ignore – to refuse to take notice of or pay attention to someone or something.

p.em: Example: Busy corporate workers often choose to ignore their body's need for relaxation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gratitude – the quality of being thankful and showing appreciation for the good things in your life.

p.em: Example: Keeping a daily journal of three good things is an excellent way to practice gratitude.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ordinary – with no special, distinctive, or unusual features; normal or standard.

p.em: Example: The quote teaches us that even an ordinary rainy day holds a quiet, simple beauty.

cosy-blockquote.p: Aware – having knowledge or conscious perception of a situation, fact, or surrounding.

p.em: Example: Being aware of your emotional state is essential to prevent feeling overwhelmed.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does our ability to notice small things determine the amount of beauty in our daily life?
★ What is the most beautiful ordinary object or scene you noticed today?

Why is practicing mindfulness more important in the digital age than ever before?
★ When was the last time you managed to experience absolute, quiet presence?

What is the difference between simply seeing something and choosing to appreciate it?
★ Who in your life shows you the most gratitude for simple, ordinary favors?

Why do we so often choose to ignore the beautiful things that are right in front of us?
★ Do you usually ignore your surroundings when you walk, or are you highly aware?

How does cultivating gratitude help us find joy in a highly stressful job?
★ What are three simple, ordinary things you are grateful for today?

Is our appreciation of aesthetic beauty in art or nature an innate or learned skill?
★ What type of natural aesthetic (forests, seas, mountains) brings you the most joy?

Why are children so much better at finding joy in completely ordinary items?
★ What was your favorite, most simple toy or game when you were a child?

How does keeping a daily gratitude journal change our perception of bad days?
★ Are you highly aware of how your attention shapes your general mood?

Can we enjoy real mental peace without learning how to slow down and practice presence?
★ Where is your favorite local place to escape and just experience quiet mindfulness?

If you could share one tip for finding more beauty in ordinary life, what would it be?
★ If you had to describe your relationship with daily gratitude in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is it easiest to practice presence and notice the ordinary beauty of life? Rank them: - 🍁 Silent Observation Sitting quietly on a park bench for ten minutes, watching the yellow autumn leaves fall. - 🎧 Rushed Walk Walking quickly to work while passively listening to an upbeat playlist on your headphones. - ☕ Morning Ritual Pausing to drink a warm cup of coffee carefully, focusing fully on the rich aroma and warmth. - 📸 Digital Capture Taking a photo of a beautiful sunset quickly to share online, instead of enjoying the moment.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, standard workspaces will enforce daily silent hours to encourage collective mindfulness. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If your boss offered "presence breaks" instead of coffee breaks, would you enjoy it?

Smart algorithms will eventually learn to design personalized, aesthetic spaces for our homes. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you trust an AI agent to decide which colors or arts bring you the most joy?

With the rise of instant notification chips, humans will completely lose their capacity to notice ordinary beauty. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think future kids will be less aware of nature than today's children?

Future homes will feature smart glasses that highlight small, beautiful ordinary things in real-time. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear glasses that help you appreciate daily life more?

As artificial intelligence automates all physical jobs, humans will focus purely on cultivating gratitude and art. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you had unlimited free time, which creative hobby would you explore with vigor?

Future generations will look back at our current busy lifestyles with deep shock and skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about the importance of daily joy to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make it incredibly difficult to experience quiet, ordinary solitude. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees safety at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by how much presence and peace a person has rather than their wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope personal mindfulness will play in your own professional future over the next decade?

A future world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the quiet mystery of individual joy. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ In what area of your life do you want to exercise greater personal presence right now?

Future smart devices will automatically filter out every distraction, leaving only quiet aesthetic peace. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic bedroom, how would you protect yourself from notifications?

ul.li: Incorrect: I want to study more hard → Correct: I want to study harder ((Comparative of 'hard' is irregular: 'harder'))
Incorrect: I am notice the leaves → Correct: I notice the leaves / I am noticing the leaves ((Simple present or present continuous structure))
Incorrect: It depend of your mind → Correct: It depends on your mind ((Verb 'depend' takes preposition 'on', and singular agreement 's'))
